title: American vs. British Piping Standards
description: US American (ASTM) vs. British (BSi) piping standards - specifications, grades and material descriptions. Compare ASTM International standards with British Standards Institute piping specifications for carbon steel, alloy steel, and stainless steel pipes.

rows: Austenitic Chromium Nickel Molybdenum (Extra Low Carbon)

components.content:
## ASTM Standard Descriptions

- **A 333** - Seamless and Welded Pipe for Low-Temperature Service
- **A 53** - Welded and Seamless Steel Pipe
- **A 106** - Seamless C-Steel Pipe for High Temperature Service
- **A 335** - Seamless Ferritic Alloy Steel Pipe for High Temperature Service
- **A 312** - Seamless and Welded Austenitic Stainless Steel Pipe
- **API 5L** - Specification for Line Pipe

## British Standards Descriptions

- **BS 1387** - Steel Tubes and Tubulars Suitable for Screwing to BS 21 Pipe Threads (Replaced by BS EN 10255:2004)
- **BS 3601** - Steel Pipes and Tubes for Pressure Purposes Carbon Steel (Replaced by BS EN 10216-1:2002 and BS EN 10217-1:2002)
- **BS 3602** - Carbon and Carbon Manganese Steel with Specified Elevated Temperature Properties (Replaced by BS EN 10216-2:2002)
- **BS 3603** - Carbon and Alloy Steel with Specified Low Temperature Properties (Replaced by EN10216-4:2002)
- **BS 3604** - Ferritic Alloy Steel with Specified Elevated Temperature Properties
- **BS 3605** - Seamless and Welded Austenitic Stainless Steel Pipe (Replaced by BS EN 10216-5:2004)
